newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia fine-tuning privatisation law - minister.
newsitem.headline: Serbia fine-tuning privatisation law - minister.

text.p: Serbia's Privatisation Ministry is readying a new version of its privatisation law to be fine-tuned within the next two weeks by the government, Privatisation Minister Milan Beko said on Wednesday.
Beko also said the ownership transformation law, which many economists already call the constitution of reforms, should soon be sent to parliament for adoption.
"We have taken into account all suggestions given to us in a public debate and continue to work on a new version of the law," the minister told reporters.
Beko said lawmakers were still considering a possibility to make the process compulsory and to make it last shorter, but no final decisions have been made yet.
"The new version of the law should not be less radical than the first version we have offered to the public. I insist that the law should serve substantial economic reforms," Beko told Reuters.
The new Serbian privatisation law was supposed to enter the parliament procedure during May, be adopted some time in June and become effective on July 1.

"There will be no backing off with adoption of reforms. There will be only some simplifications and improvement of the document based on suggestions given by economic experts," Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic told Reuters. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
